author: LucaPacioselli
body:
#### PR description:

This PR converts `MPIController` into a `global` module allowing multiple transitions to be sent concurrently to `MPISource`. The `MPISource` module has been adapted accordingly.

The main changes are:

* Introduce per-stream cache in `MPIController`, consisting of a dedicated control channel and a pool of data channels. The current implementation uses 3 data channels per stream.
* Redesign `MPISource` around a dedicated control thread and one receiver thread per controller stream assigned to the follower. These threads are separated from framework threads.
* Decouple MPI communication from framework thread by buffering received events in per (run-lumi) queues. Receiver threads populate these `tbb::concurrent_queue`s, while `setRunAndEventInfo()` consumes them.
* Preserve the ordering of luminosity blocks seen by the `MPISource` using the ordered (run-lumi) queues. A queue is considered complete only after the corresponding `globalEndLuminosityBlock()` transition is received from the `MPIController` and will be released after being drained.

#### PR validation:

The code in this PR has been tested with the existing `MPICore` tests. 

To verify that `MPIController` could handle more runs and luminosity blocks at a time, I ran the [controller_cfg.py](https://github.com/cms-sw/cmssw/blob/master/HeterogeneousCore/MPICore/test/controller_cfg.py) test with `numberOfConcurrentLuminosityBlocks` and `numberOfConcurrentRuns` greater than one, one event per luminosity block, and a number of streams greater than the number of luminosity blocks in a run.
title: Convert MPIController into a global EDProducer
